newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Low priced Tapis sold to US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Low priced Tapis sold to US Gulf.

text.p: The Asian light crude market remained steady despite news of Malaysian Tapis and Miri sold to US Gulf at very low levels, traders said on Monday.
"August market is almost finished, so the impact is limited" said a trader.
A 900,000 barrel combi cargo of August Tapis and Miri was confirmed traded between majors last week, scheduled to arrive in the US Gulf by mid September.
Traders initially heard that the deal involved 900,000 barrels of Tapis crude alone.
The Tapis was done at WTI +10 cents per barrel, while Miri was at WTI +23 cents on a cost and freight (c+f) basis.
With freight estimated around $2.00, traders equate the Tapis price to be a discount of almost $1.00 under APPI.

But sellers of September light crudes were offering higher levels, expecting improved demand, since there were limited West African cargoes arriving in that period. Oman trades dominated the Middle East crude market. Several September cargoes of Oman changed hands, but prices were varied widely. "The market is confused. I have no idea where the next trade will be done at" said a western trader.

An Oman equity producer heard bought three cargoes, two from separate shosha at MPM -19, and MPM -20, and the third from a western trader at MPM -19. But two cargoes were also heard sold to a western trader, at MPM -13 and MPM -11.
